articles.title: Death Stranding Isolations Anime Gets First Trailer
articles.summary: Kojima Productions revealed the first trailer for Death Stranding Isolations, an original anime series set in the world of Death Stranding, scheduled to release on Disney+ next year. The news was shared in a tweet late on October 29 (the morning of October 30 in Japan).
body: The tweet itself doesn't provide any more clarity; in the post, a quote reads, "My mom became a crater."

Death Stranding Isolations is promised to be an original story driven by its "own unique ensemble of characters," suggesting that Sam Porter Bridges, Fragile, and co. won't be major players in the narrative.

As previously announced, the series will stream exclusively on Disney+ in 2027, though no exact date was given. The anime is directed by Takayuki Sano, known for doing the key animation, as well as designing creatures and props, directing, and many other duties for a swath of major anime over the years. Most notably, he served as the animation director for Attack on Titan's final season, as well as episodes of Jujutsu Kaisen and the movie Jujutsu Kaisen 0.

Tow Ubukata is set to compose the series and its screenplay. Ubukata is a noted science fiction author who lent his talents to Psycho-Pass 3 and Psycho-Pass: Providence, Ghost in the Shell: The New Movie, and was the Free Scenario Plotter for Shenmue.

articles.title: Attack on Titan 3: The Final Preview
articles.summary: Attack on Titan 3 may come with a number, but it isn’t a direct sequel in the truest sense of the word. It’s more of a retelling. Based on my time with it, Attack on Titan 3 is juggling a lot of plates, and its ambition to do something new with the franchise is pretty laudable.
body: I must confess something before I get this preview started: I bowed out of Attack on Titan early. After the first season, actually. I didn’t think it was terrible or anything. I was there for the human drama. Little people swinging around like Spider-Man and dealing with their trauma while playing a game of David and Goliath against big, scary Titans. But when those little dudes started being able to become Titans, well… it just wasn’t for me. But after spending some time with Attack on Titan 3 and speaking to producer Hideo Suzuki, I’m tempted to give it another go… at least as a video game.

But I have to get to know these kids, too. Attack on Titan is probably most famous for its high-flying human vs. Titan battles or its knock down, drag out Titan-on-Titan brawls, but it’s a human story at heart, and building relationships with the other characters is a core part of Attack on Titan 3.
points: Attack on Titan 3 may come with a number, but it isn’t a direct sequel in the truest sense of the word.
Based on my time with it, Attack on Titan 3 is juggling a lot of plates, and its ambition to do something new with the franchise is pretty laudable.

articles.title: Patrick Stewart Dies At 86
articles.summary: Beloved actor Patrick Stewart has died at the age of 86. The veteran of stage and screen was best known for his many years as Star Trek's Jean-Luc Picard and X-Men's Charles Xavier, though he also had notable roles in video games, including The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion and Castlevania: Lords of…
body: "We announce with grew sorrow the passing of Sir Patrick Stewart yesterday at his home in Los Angeles, in the loving care of his beloved wife Sunny, following a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer's Disease and Lewy Body Dimentia" a statement on his official Instagram reads. "He has been held in the warm embrace of family and friends, surrounded by live music, prayer, tears, laughter, and the kind of profound emotion that only he could inspire after a lifetime of devotion to us all. We will forever cherish the peaceful ease and reflection on his face, an enduring reminder of his invincible grace."

Stewart's role as Picard made him a household name, and following the conclusion of Star Trek: The Next Generation, he reprised the role in several Star Trek films as well as the series Star Trek: Picard.

articles.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Adds 'Non MilSim Content' Disclaimer to Halloween Themed Content
articles.summary: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 has added new disclaimers to content that may not abide by the game's usual grounded tone and aesthetic. Earlier today, Modern Warfare 4 added a new mode known as Possession.
body: This comes after years of players getting frustrated that Call of Duty's multiplayer often abandons the darker, more serious tone established by the campaign and seasonal lore drops. The franchise has added skins that allow players to play as Nicki Minaj, Beavis and Butthead, and Seth Rogen, which has come at the cost of the game's identity. Infinity Ward already promised to dial things back with Modern Warfare 4 and not include absurd, over-the-top skins, but this new disclaimer does suggest there will be some content that may ride a line for hardcore fans.

Of course, you can also make the argument that Call of Duty isn't realistic and it isn't really a "milsim" game, since it's so fast-paced and filled with ridiculous movement, Wolverine-style health regeneration, and more. It's more of an aesthetic than a style of play. Still, some players value the immersion of more realistic military characters and modes and don't want that disrupted.

articles.title: Gears of War: E-Day Reportedly Sold Over 400K Copies Across Console and PC a Month After Day-One Game Pass Launch
articles.summary: Sources tell The Verge that Gears of War: E-Day has sold over 400,000 copies across console and PC, and Game Pass is likely to blame. The latest entry in the Gears franchise released to critical acclaim earlier this month, drawing high scores from reviewers and fans alike.
body: However, it seems the title’s popularity isn’t translating to sales — at least, that’s according to a new figure reported by The Verge. Correspondent Tom Warren cited a source who estimated that 400,000 copies of the game have been sold in total across consoles and PC, which paints a grim figure considering the prestige of this particular release.

Data from Alinea Analytics appears to corroborate this thought. As laid out in an October 9 post from the research firm’s head of market analysis, Rhys Elliott, an estimated 1.7 million players accessed E-Day using their Game Pass subscription, rather than buying a copy.

Elliott figured that of those 1.7 million players, likely 722,000 paid for the Premium upgrade, with the game prompting an additional 250,000 Premium upgrades between October 1 and the game’s full release on October 6.

articles.title: WoW: Forever Won’t Have Dead Servers
articles.summary: World of Warcraft: Forever will avoid repeating WoW Classic's mistakes and will have tools to prevent "dead" or "unsustainable" server rulesets, Blizzard said. In the past, various WoW Classic servers became "dead" over time, as players either stopped playing or transferred to other servers.
body: While Forever is going a different route with what are essentially mega servers tailored around specific rulesets, some players might still have anxiety when it comes to picking a ruleset that will be a healthy place to play long-term.

In the latest episode of the WoW: Forever podcast, Blizzard said it has tools it can use if a ruleset's population becomes "unsustainable." Senior game designer Josh Greenfield gave the example of Forever's separate RP and (newly added) RP-PvP server rulesets. He said there were initially concerns about splitting up the RP community, fearing that one or both of the rulesets wouldn't be able to stand the test of time. He said Blizzard now believes "it will be fine," but does have options should the worst happen.

"If someday down the line, if something happens and one or both of those populations can't quite sustain themselves, we have options if we do need to say link up their auction houses or allow them to group for instanced content," Greenfield said.
points: World of Warcraft: Forever will avoid repeating WoW Classic's mistakes and will have tools to prevent "dead" or "unsustainable" server rulesets, Blizzard said.

articles.title: Artist With Music In GTA 6 Had No Idea About Any Of That
articles.summary: Cliff Richard is among the numerous famous artists who are lending their music to Rockstar's GTA 6, with Richard's classic tune "Devil Woman" appearing in the Netflix Extended Look. Richard, 86, didn't know about any of that, however, or that GTA 6 is a game and not a TV show.
body: Speaking to The Times ( via Dexerto ), Richard said of the partnership with Rockstar for GTA 6: "I was told this happened!" He said his nephew's sons told him about it. "They didn't realize I could sing like that," he said.
Richard was eventually made aware of GTA 6, but the singer doesn't know what that is. “The show is a game show, isn’t it, really? One of the biggest on TV?” he asked.
"Devil Woman" was originally released in 1976, so it's now 50 years old. Richard said he's pretty jazzed about the fact that young people will hear his music.
“People will no longer just say, ‘Oh, Cliff Richard is from the past,’” he said. “Because I am, but that past is what makes everything what it is today."

articles.title: Official The Elder Scrolls 6 Announcement Imminent, Report Says
articles.summary: The Elder Scrolls fans know that Bethesda is hard at work on the next highly anticipated roleplaying game entry, The Elder Scrolls 6, but that's about it. The lack of concrete information is wild when you consider that the sequel to The Elder Scrolls 5: Skyrim was announced a whopping eight years…
body: To be fair to Bethesda, the studio does occasionally acknowledge The Elder Scrolls 6 publicly. In 2025, for example, the developer revealed that the secretive open-world game was already fully playable. The next year, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma implied that TES 6 was a fun time. Bethesda has also said that, despite teases of a new Fallout game, the studio was still primarily focused on Skyrim 's sequel.

Despite this ongoing radio silence, The Verge reports that Bethesda's marketing is about to turn up a notch. A new dispatch from the tech site claims that Bethesda will officially announce the game's apparent title — The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel — sometime around the fifteen-year anniversary (!) for Skyrim. For those who just turned to dust, Skyrim released on Nov. 11, 2011, so that's coming up.

The report further states that the new Elder Scrolls game will take place in Hammerfell, and that it will cover the history of the Elder Scrolls themselves. Much like in Starfield, players will be uncovering the secrets of mysterious ancient artifacts.

articles.title: Ubisoft Issues Official Update on Fate of Future Assassin's Creed Remakes
articles.summary: Ubisoft's latest Assassin's Creed game was a blast from the past. Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced is a remake of the 2013 pirate adventure. As remakes become more and more common in the industry, fans have naturally wondered if more Assassin's Creed remakes are in the pipeline.
body: His use of the plural "remakes" hinted at remakes other than just Black Flag Resynced, but Ubisoft has now confirmed the status of other Assassin's Creed games under active development.

On Thursday, Ubisoft updated fans on the status of the franchise, and touched on fan demand for additional remakes. "One thing we want to be transparent about today is that we currently have no other Assassin's Creed remake actively in development," Ubisoft said. "Our teams are already focused on the next chapter of Assassin's Creed titles, including projects you haven't heard about yet, featuring new settings and stories."

However, just because they're not actively being worked on, don't rule out the possibility of more remakes, or rereleases, sometime in the future. "Like many of you, we love the idea of revisiting our classic titles, and we'll keep exploring opportunities to bring older titles back. That door remains open because, after all... Nothing is true, everything is permitted," Ubisoft said, referencing the oft-repeated Assassin maxim.

articles.title: Patrick Stewart's Greatest Captain Picard Quote Is Still a Defining Star Trek Moment
articles.summary: Every Star Trek fan has an opinion on the franchise's greatest captain. Some prefer the swagger of James T. Kirk (William Shatner). Others admire Benjamin Sisko (Avery Brooks) for his conviction, or Kathryn Janeway (Kate Mulgrew) for her resilience.
body: To celebrate the life of Sir Patrick Stewart, Polygon is republishing this tribute to his seminal performance as Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek: The Next Generation.

Not surprisingly, the Stewart quote that best captures why Jean-Luc Picard remains so beloved isn't about command. It isn't, "Make it so." It isn't, "Engage." It isn't even, "Darmok and Jalad at Tanagra," although I absolutely want that on a T-shirt. The best words Picard ever utters come quietly near the end of The Next Generation's fifth-season masterpiece, "The Inner Light."
"Seize the time... Live now. Make now always the most precious time. Now will never come again."

It's the greatest quote Jean-Luc Picard ever speaks because it explains the man beneath the captain's uniform better than any order he ever gave from the bridge of the Enterprise. Oddly enough, he isn't Jean-Luc Picard when he says it.
points: Every Star Trek fan has an opinion on the franchise's greatest captain.

articles.title: Reddit will switch to a 'logged-in only experience'
articles.summary: Reddit will become a "logged-in only experience," and the company plans to move fast, beginning testing soon in regions outside the US before flipping the switch globally.
body: The popular community website—home to a great many official and unofficial gaming message boards—lost one million search engine referrals per week on average in October, CEO Steve Huffman said on an investor call today.

The culprit, of course, was AI. A Google search that once might have led someone to a 14-year-old Reddit thread containing the answer to a rare household cleaning problem is now likely to present that answer in an AI summary, no click required.
"Google has really shifted in their relationship with the rest of the internet," Huffman said during a Q&A.

The CEO emphasized, however, that most of Reddit's revenue (over 80%) comes from logged-in and app users, and said that the company will focus on establishing the site as "a direct daily habit" that doesn't rely on search traffic.
points: Reddit will become a "logged-in only experience," and the company plans to move fast, beginning testing soon in regions outside the US before flipping the switch globally.

articles.title: Square Enix should never make a Final Fantasy game without turn-based combat again
articles.summary: I had few expectations going into Final Fantasy Resonance, the premium game based on Square Enix's mobile gacha Brave Exvius. Those expectations lowered in the first 10 hours, thanks to its frankly atrocious writing.
body: Whatever Resonance 's faults, and there are many, it's a Final Fantasy game that cares little for anything outside itself. It's not struggling with some existential crisis about what a Final Fantasy game needs to be, or how to make it “relevant” for modern audiences. There's no craven devotion to the past or some vaguely formed notion of legacy. It's arguably even less concerned with legacy than Bravely Default, which, despite some clever uses of classic Final Fantasy, still relies heavily on the series' bygone era.

Okay, there's some craven devotion to the past in Resonance, like when it throws out "spoony bard" or other painfully on-the-nose references. But once it settles into its groove after the mid-game, Resonance is just itself, for better and worse. Multiple planets? Witches turning into chocobos? Zombies, magic, and science coexisting without anyone batting an eye? Sure, why not. Anything goes, and Resonance is confident enough in its own logic to tie everything together so it feels natural instead of discordant.
points: I had few expectations going into Final Fantasy Resonance, the premium game based on Square Enix's mobile gacha Brave Exvius.

articles.title: 'None of these people have ever made a game,' BioWare co-founder Greg Zeschuk says of game industry executives: 'They just don't know how it works'
articles.summary: It's been almost 15 years since BioWare co-founders Greg Zeschuk and Ray Muzyka announced their retirements from the videogame industry, and they've been resolute about staying out of it ever since: Muzyka continues to head up the ThresholdImpact investment firm he founded in 2012 and holds…
body: But Zeschuk stepped back into the videogame spotlight, briefly, following last week's closure of BioWare by parent company Electronic Arts, telling 80lv that he got the news hours after it happened because he was on a fishing trip, and by the time he flew home a couple days later, he'd "already shelved it away."

"I wasn't there to share in the moment, which in some ways was nice because I was able to kind of just take my time with it," Zeschuk said. "I’m not saying it doesn't hurt and doesn't suck. And I think it's kind of sad. It's actually, in some ways, saddest for the city of Edmonton, where we're from, because we were kind of this beacon of hope and excitement and possibility. We showed you could do something really special in a place that was not known for doing things like that."

Zeschuk said he had his own "emotional moment" about BioWare years ago, when he left the company; his real concern now is for the people at the studio who now find themselves out of work: "Anyone getting put into the job hunt is a sort of terrifying endeavor and super sad."

videos.title: DF Direct Q+A: Has RTX 5090 Actually Been Discontinued? GTA 6 PS5/Pro Differences?
videos.summary: Thanks to Alienware for sponsoring DF Direct. To learn more about the Alienware AREA-51 Gaming Desktop, check out:
body: Reports that Nvidia's RTX 5090 gaming flagship would be discontinued gathered pace, with Nvidia finally denying cancellation of the card. But in a world where a 5090 can cost $8000, is its presence in the gaming market all but over? Can Nvidia do anything about it? Meanwhile, DF Supporter have questions about GTA 6 on PlayStation and in the absence of actual information, we can only offer our thoughts and speculation. Finally, what would actually constitute a Switch 2 "impossible port"...?
